notes.inflation: Inflation is the EU's harmonised index (HICP), the measure the ECB targets, which can differ by a few tenths from Statbel's national CPI used for wage indexation. Belgium has no policy rate of its own: the rate shown is the European Central Bank's deposit facility rate, set for the whole euro area.
notes.labour: Unemployment is Eurostat's monthly, seasonally adjusted rate (ILO definition, ages 15 to 74). Employment and participation rates are the OECD's quarterly figures for ages 15 to 64.
notes.trade: Goods trade is Eurostat's monthly total with the rest of the world, in euros. Belgium is a transit hub, so goods passing through the port of Antwerp-Bruges count in both directions, and figures on other concepts can differ by a few billion.
notes.public: Debt and the budget balance are Eurostat's excessive deficit procedure figures for general government (federal, regions, communities and local authorities), calendar years, so the latest year is a year ahead of the IMF's.
notes.markets: The 10-year yield is the OECD's monthly average of the Belgian government (OLO) yield; the exchange rates are the Federal Reserve's daily euro rates, shared with every euro area page.
